name: queryResult.py
summary: Django ORM model that persists the output data of executed queries and links results to their corresponding query execution history.
purpose: Provides a persistent storage layer for query execution outcomes, enabling retrieval, auditing, and serialization of query results independently from the execution metadata stored in QueryHistory.
responsibilities: Store query execution output data and metadata
Maintain a relationship to QueryHistory for traceability
Support repository and serializer layers for data access and API presentation
Enable administrative visibility via Django admin integration
inputs: Query execution output (e.g., result sets, status, format)
Django ORM model field definitions and migrations
outputs: Serialized query response data via query_response.py
Domain objects for the queries repository layer
architecture_notes: Implements the Active Record pattern via Django's ORM. It is positioned in the domain/data layer of a layered architecture, decoupled from presentation logic through the repository and serializer neighbors. The explicit separation between QueryHistory (execution metadata/audit) and QueryResult (output payload) suggests a design favoring single-responsibility storage, though it introduces a required join or relationship traversal for full context.
improvements: Add database indexes on foreign keys and frequently filtered fields (e.g., created_at, query_history_id) to improve retrieval performance
Consider extracting large result payloads to object storage or a separate JSONB/NoSQL store if result sizes grow significantly
Implement a custom manager or repository method to avoid N+1 queries when fetching results alongside their history
Add explicit ordering (Meta.ordering) and verbose names for better admin and API usability
Evaluate whether the model should be immutable (e.g., prevent updates) if query results are meant to be historical snapshots
